data.narrative:
Pickle Robot Company is a Series B robotics and manufacturing startup that has raised $97M to date. The valuation analysis leverages a peer set of 3 same-sector, same-stage private companies (Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, and Dexterity) alongside 1 public comparable, reflecting a broader universe of 9 private peers in the robotics space.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method, using total raised as a valuation proxy, applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yielding $184M. The peer-median approach benchmarks against the three identified comparables, which trade at a median valuation of $1.8B with a range of $1.6B to $2.0B. This method reflects current market pricing for similar-stage robotics companies.

The triangulated analysis produces a range of $157M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $967M. The wide spread reflects material methodological divergence: stage-progression anchors conservatively to capital deployed, while peer-median reflects recent private market pricing for analogous businesses. Key uncertainties include capital efficiency relative to peers, revenue traction and unit economics relative to the comparables, and the relevance of the single public comparable. Resolution of these factors—particularly relative growth trajectory and path to profitability—will materially influence placement within the $157M–$2.0B band.
